name: iZEV federal rebate
notes: Program closed. It has not been reinstated as iZEV. Transport Canada now points users to EVAP (Electric Vehicle Affordability Program) for current federal light-duty EV incentives.

name: Electric Vehicle Affordability Program (EVAP)
notes: BEV/FCEV federal rebate up to $5,000. Final transaction value (MSRP + freight/PDI + accessories + dealer fees, pre-tax) must be $50,000 or less for imported EVs (E-GMP cars are made in Korea/US so the cap applies). No cap for Canadian-made EVs. Lease term prorates: 48mo+ gets full $5,000; 36mo $3,750; 24mo $2,500; 12mo $1,250.

name: Zero Emission Vehicle Infrastructure Program (ZEVIP)
notes: Infrastructure contribution funding for eligible organizations/projects, not a direct individual home-charger rebate. Funding stream, intake, charger type, and applicant category determine the amount.

name: CleanBC Go Electric passenger vehicle rebate
notes: Passenger vehicle rebate page states the program is currently paused.

name: CleanBC Go Electric home charger rebate
notes: Up to 50% of eligible Level 2 charger installation cost, capped at $350, for single-family homes, duplexes, triplexes, or other semi-detached housing. Eligible charger and utility-provider application rules apply.

name: Roulez vert new BEV rebate
notes: Fully electric vehicles registered in 2026 are listed at $2,000. Program ends December 31, 2026. Eligibility depends on vehicle/version and registration date. Vehicles registered during the February 1 to March 31, 2025 suspension period were not eligible.

name: Plug-In NB EV rebate
notes: Program guidelines state Plug-In NB closed June 30, 2025 and would not be extended. Former BEV amount was $5,000 for eligible purchases or 48-month leases.

name: Plug-In NB Level 2 home charging station rebate
notes: Former rebate was 50% of eligible purchase + installation cost before taxes/delivery, capped at $750, only for participants in the Plug-In NB EV rebate program. Program has ended.

name: Electrify Nova Scotia light-duty EV rebate
notes: Nova Scotia government progress report states Electrify NS has ended rebates for light-duty EVs and e-bikes. Medium- and heavy-duty zero-emission vehicle rebates are separate and not applicable to EV6/Ioniq5/Ioniq6 personal light-duty purchases.

name: TakeCharge listed NLCU Eco-Friendly Vehicle Loan Rebate
notes: TakeCharge currently lists an NLCU loan rebate, not a provincial point-of-sale vehicle rebate. Hybrid or electric vehicle must be five years old or newer; rebate is 2.5% or 3% depending on NLCU banking setup, capped at $1,500.

name: PEI Universal EV Incentive
notes: Eligible BEVs receive $4,000 and PHEVs receive $2,000 as of June 2, 2025. Lease amounts are prorated: BEV 48+ months $4,000, 36 months $3,000, 24 months $2,000, 12 months $1,000. Teslas no longer eligible as of March 25, 2025.

name: Yukon Good Energy light-duty zero-emission vehicle rebate
notes: Electric transportation rebates ended March 31, 2026. Applications remain possible only for purchases made on or before March 31, 2026. Former BEV / long-range PHEV amount was $5,000.

name: Manitoba Electric Vehicle Rebate Program
notes: Manitoba is not a no-rebate province. Official program page lists $4,000 for eligible new EVs and $2,500 for eligible pre-owned EVs. Model and transaction eligibility must be checked against Manitoba program criteria.

name: Ontario Electric and Hydrogen Vehicle Incentive Program
notes: Ontario cancelled the Electric and Hydrogen Vehicle Incentive Program on July 11, 2018. No current Ontario provincial light-duty EV purchase rebate was found on official Ontario / IESO sources.

name: Alberta light-duty EV purchase rebate
notes: No active Alberta light-duty EV purchase rebate identified. Official Alberta page instead lists a $200 annual electric vehicle tax for battery electric vehicles.

name: Saskatchewan light-duty EV purchase rebate
notes: No active Saskatchewan light-duty EV purchase rebate identified. Official Saskatchewan page lists an annual road-use charge on Class LV EVs: $300 from June 1, 2025 to December 31, 2026.

name: Northwest Territories light-duty EV rebate
notes: GNWT page states that as of 2025-26, GNWT core funding for rebates has ended. Rebates may still be available directly through Arctic Energy Alliance, but a current official AEA vehicle-rebate amount was not confirmed from the current rebate index.

name: Northwest Territories Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Program
notes: Infrastructure program supports charging installations in public places, street parking, multi-unit residential buildings, workplaces, and light-duty fleet facilities. Search result lists maximum of $99,999 per Level 3 fast charger. Not a direct personal home-charger rebate.

name: Nunavut light-duty EV purchase rebate
notes: No active Nunavut government light-duty EV purchase or EV-charger installation rebate was found on official Nunavut government sources. Search results returned carbon/electricity rebate material, not an EV purchase incentive.

name: Save On Energy EV charger installation rebate
notes: No current Save On Energy direct EV-charger installation rebate found. Current Save On Energy business programs list energy-efficiency programs; EV-charger fact sheets point to other funding sources rather than a Save On Energy EV charger rebate.

name: Enbridge Smart Home EV charger eligibility
notes: No EV-charger eligibility found on Enbridge Ontario rebate pages. Home Efficiency Rebate intake ended January 27, 2025 and current Enbridge / Home Renovation Savings materials focus on home energy-efficiency upgrades, not EV chargers.

name: Kia EV6 — current monthly offers (verify on kia.ca)
notes: Kia Canada special-offers page is current but EV6 cash / APR / residual / monthly fields were not exposed in retrievable official text. Check the source URL for the live offer; values change monthly.

name: Hyundai Ioniq 5 — current monthly offers (verify on hyundaicanada.com)
notes: Hyundai Canada special-offers page did not expose Ioniq 5 cash / APR / residual / monthly fields in retrievable official text. Check the source URL for the live offer; values change monthly.

name: Hyundai Ioniq 6 Preferred — current monthly offers
notes: Hyundai Canada EV incentives page lists Ioniq 6 eligible models and total incentive ranges, but only explicitly identifies the $16,000 Hyundai Special Offer Bonus as available on the Ultimate Package. Exact Preferred non-Ultimate manufacturer cash / APR / residual / monthly fields were not exposed in retrievable text — verify at the source.

name: Hyundai Ioniq 6 Ultimate Package Special Offer Bonus
notes: Hyundai Canada EV incentives page states the Ioniq 6 incentive amount is based on EVAP $5,000, Hyundai Special Offer Bonus $16,000 available on the Ultimate Package, and provincial incentive available in Manitoba and PEI ($4,000). APR / residual / monthly lease and finance examples were not exposed in official retrievable text. Note: 'Ultimate Package' in Hyundai marketing maps closely to the 'Limited AWD' trim in the dealer inventory taxonomy — verify at delivery.

name: Kia EV9 — current monthly offers (verify on kia.ca)
notes: Late-April 2026 captured 401 Dixie Kia EV9 listings showed an explicit $2,000 dealer incentive on Light RWD inventory. Treat as observed dealer-side cash; verify live values monthly.

name: Hyundai Ioniq 9 — current monthly offers (verify on hyundaicanada.com)
notes: Ioniq 9 launched MY2026; live cash/APR fields not yet captured. Check source URL for current month.

name: Hyundai Loyalty Incentive — Ioniq 5/6/9
notes: Current Hyundai or Genesis owner loyalty benefit: (a) $500 after-tax cash rebate on cash purchase, OR (b) 0.5% finance rate reduction (floor 0%), OR (c) 2.0% lease rate reduction (floor 0%). Cash rebate and rate reduction cannot be combined. Owner or immediate family member at same address with proof of ownership. Valid across all new Hyundai models incl. Ioniq 5/6/9. aprPercent here represents the finance rate reduction; lease rate reduction is 2.0% (not separately modelled in schema).

name: Hyundai Conquest Cash — Ioniq 5/6/9
notes: Hyundai Canada conquest cash for competing-brand owners switching to an Ioniq EV. Exact CAD amount not publicly disclosed on hyundaicanada.com — dealers apply it as a hidden incentive. Ask dealer to apply conquest cash; require proof of current competing-brand ownership/lease at time of purchase. amountCad omitted pending official confirmation; flag as negotiation lever.

name: Kia Loyalty Rate Reduction — EV6/EV9
notes: Current Kia owner or lessee earns an extra 1% off the published finance or lease rate when financing/leasing a new Kia through Kia Finance. Existing Kia must be registered and insured in the customer's name for ≥90 days prior to purchase date. Each qualifying VIN may only be used once within a 180-day period. Rate reduction cannot take the rate below 0%. aprPercent here represents the rate reduction amount. Stacks with most manufacturer credits, graduate, military, and mobility programs.

name: Kia Conquest — EV6/EV9
notes: Kia Canada conquest program for competing-brand owners. Exact CAD amount not publicly disclosed on kia.ca for May 2026. US Kia conquest (per kalidykia.com) was $500–$1,000 in Jul 2025 for EV9. Ask dealer to apply conquest cash; require proof of current competing-brand ownership/lease. amountCad omitted pending official Canadian confirmation.

name: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Preferred RWD LR — May 2026 Lease
notes: Hyundai Financial Services national lease program. 3.79% APR, 60-month walk-away lease, $0 security deposit, 16,000 km/yr, $0.12/km overage. Weekly lease payment $153; monthly equivalent $153×4.33 ≈ $663 (pre-tax). $0 down. Source is Central Nova Hyundai re-publishing HFS national disclaimer. residualPercent=48% back-calculated from disclaimer's total obligation $39,778 / cap-cost $58,473 (incl. admin) on 2026-05-02 — Hyundai Canada does not publish residual tables; corroborated by Ioniq Forum Canada thread on 2022-era Preferred Long Range RWD leases reporting ~49% at 39mo. Confidence: Medium (±2pp). When dashboard's compute uses cap = MSRP+freight only (no admin), the resulting monthly is ~$649 vs dealer's $663 — acceptable modeling delta for personal-use.

name: Hyundai Ioniq 5 Preferred RWD LR — May 2026 Finance
notes: Hyundai Financial Services national finance program. 2.59% APR for 84 months, $0 down. Selling price in disclaimer: $64,270 (incl. freight/PDI $2,050, admin $599). Weekly payment $177; monthly equivalent $177×4.33 ≈ $767 (pre-tax). Cost of borrowing $5,797.

name: Kia EV6 — May 2026 Finance
notes: Kia Canada May 2026 subvented finance on 2026 EV6: 0.99% APR up to 60 months OAC through Kia Finance, RBC, or TD Auto Finance. Rates may vary by term length and creditworthiness. Before applying 1% loyalty reduction (which would take to 0% floor). Confirmed at multiple Ontario Kia dealers for May 1–June 1, 2026.

name: Kia EV9 Light RWD — May 2026 Lease
notes: Kia Canada May 2026 subvented lease on 2026 EV9 Light RWD: 3.19% APR, 36-month walk-away lease, 16,000 km/yr. Biweekly payment $374; monthly equivalent $374×2.17 ≈ $811. $0 down. MSRP base $59,995. Confirmed via Applewood Kia Surrey listing. Before applying 1% loyalty reduction. residualPercent=63% back-calculated 2026-05-02 from Applewood fine print (biweekly $374, 36mo, 3.19%, MSRP $59,995, total obligation ~$29,162) and corroborated against US Edmunds/Reddit data for EV9 Light Long Range 36mo (63–64%). Kia Canada does not publish residual tables. Confidence: Medium (±2pp).
